title: Headache
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with severe headache, blurred vision, and severely elevated blood pressure (>180/120). This is a hypertensive emergency — severe hypertension WITH evidence of acute end-organ damage (headache/visual changes suggesting cerebral involvement, possible papilledema, retinal hemorrhages). Must be distinguished from hypertensive urgency (severe HTN without end-organ damage — manage with oral meds as outpatient). Workup: fundoscopy (papilledema, hemorrhages, exudates), ECG (LVH, ischemia), CXR (pulmonary edema, aortic dissection signs), UA (proteinuria, hematuria), BMP (elevated Cr — renal damage), cardiac enzymes, CT head if focal neuro deficits. Treatment: IV antihypertensives in ICU — reduce MAP by no more than 25% in first hour (too rapid reduction causes cerebral/coronary hypoperfusion). Labetalol IV, nicardipine, or clevidipine. Goal: reduce DBP to 100-105 over 2-6 hours. Do NOT use short-acting nifedipine (risk of rapid uncontrollable hypotension).
chief_complaint: Severe headache, blurry vision, severely elevated BP

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Heart / Cardiovascular
stacks.finding: Hypertensive emergency → assess for LVH, S4, new murmurs.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Neuro / Psych
stacks.finding: Headache + visual changes — assess for focal deficits, altered mental status.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Fundoscopy
stacks.finding: Papilledema, retinal hemorrhages, cotton wool spots, AV nicking — signs of end-organ damage.

stacks.label: BMP / CMP
stacks.finding: Creatinine — assess for acute kidney injury from hypertensive damage.

stacks.label: CT head without contrast
stacks.finding: Rule out intracranial hemorrhage if focal neuro deficits or AMS.

stacks.label: IV Labetalol / Nicardipine / Clevidipine
stacks.finding: IV antihypertensive. Reduce MAP by ≤25% in first hour. Goal DBP 100-105 over 2-6h. Do NOT rapidly normalize BP.

stacks.label: Admit to ICU
stacks.finding: Hypertensive emergency requires ICU for continuous BP monitoring and IV therapy.

physical_exam.cardiovascular: Severely elevated BP >180/120. S4 gallop (LVH). Assess for aortic regurgitation murmur (dissection).
physical_exam.neurological: Headache, blurry vision. No focal deficits. Assess for altered mental status.

decoys.label: Short-acting nifedipine PO
decoys.reason_wrong: Rapid, uncontrollable hypotension → cerebral and coronary hypoperfusion → stroke and MI. NEVER use short-acting nifedipine for hypertensive emergency.

decoys.label: Rapid BP normalization to 120/80
decoys.reason_wrong: Reduce MAP by ≤25% in first hour. Rapid normalization causes cerebral hypoperfusion (loss of autoregulation). Goal DBP 100-105 over 2-6 hours.

teach_me_steps.order: Hypertensive emergency = severe HTN + end-organ damage
teach_me_steps.reasoning: Headache + visual changes + papilledema = cerebral end-organ damage. Fundoscopy + ECG + UA + Cr + troponin + CT head. Emergency ≠ urgency (no end-organ damage).

teach_me_steps.order: IV labetalol: slow, controlled BP reduction
teach_me_steps.reasoning: Reduce MAP by ≤25% in first hour. Goal DBP 100-105 over 2-6h. ICU for continuous monitoring. NEVER short-acting nifedipine.

case_summary: Hypertensive emergency with cerebral end-organ damage (headache + visual changes + papilledema). IV labetalol in ICU. Reduce MAP ≤25% in first hour. Avoid rapid normalization.
